title: Bangladesh, Denmark to shape new partnership beyond 2028
excerpt: Bangladesh and Denmark will start work in 2027 on a cooperation framework for after 2028, UNB reports. Denmark reaffirmed aid for Rohingya refugees.
content:
DHAKA, 28 November 2026: Bangladesh and Denmark have agreed to begin a process in 2027 to define a framework for their cooperation after 2028, when the current partnership plan ends, the news agency UNB reported on Friday (27 November), citing the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

The decision came at the fourth round of political consultations between the two countries in Dhaka on Thursday (26 November). The talks were co-chaired by Dr Md Nazrul Islam, Secretary (East-West) at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and Elsebeth Søndergaard Krone, Denmark's State Secretary for International Partnerships. The new process will build on the Sustainable and Green Framework Engagement and its Joint Action Plan for 2023-2028, and will reflect the growing role of trade and investment in the relationship, UNB said.

Bangladesh called Denmark an important development partner and stressed the need for predictable, long-term market access for a smooth transition, according to the ministry. The two sides discussed cooperation in climate adaptation, renewable energy, water management, the circular economy, sustainable agriculture, maritime affairs and education, as well as migration management and skills, with a focus on safe and regular migration. They agreed to move ahead with a proposed Bangladesh-Denmark Trade and Investment Committee.

The two sides welcomed a renewed government-to-government memorandum on public-private partnership and an agreement on Component II of the Saidabad Water Treatment Plant Phase III project, which UNB described as a revised procurement strategy for DKK 2.4 billion (about EUR 300 million) supported by Impact Fund Denmark. The project aims to improve access to safe drinking water in Dhaka. They also welcomed a memorandum between the Asian University for Women and APM Terminals on internships, jobs and maritime education for women.

Denmark reaffirmed its humanitarian support for Rohingya refugees and host communities. Both sides welcomed the International Court of Justice judgment in The Gambia v. Myanmar and called for full compliance with it. The fifth round will be held in Copenhagen in 2027.

Why it matters

Denmark is one of the European donors whose support covers climate, water, rights and the Rohingya response. A shift towards trade and investment in the next framework could change how much goes to grants for civil society and services, at a time when aid pledges are rising but NGOs are shrinking. Its renewed Rohingya commitment matters as other donors cut back; see Devlens on what the ICJ ruling can and cannot change.

What to watch

  • The 2027 process to set the post-2028 framework, and whether civil society is consulted.
  • Progress on the Saidabad Phase III water project.
  • Any new Danish humanitarian pledges for the 2027 Rohingya response plan.

Sources

  • UNB: Bangladesh, Denmark to initiate a process in 2027 to define framework for cooperation beyond 2028, 27 November 2026
